templates.incident-triage.name: Incident triage → GitHub + Slack
templates.incident-triage.description: Webhook receives an incident, AI summarizes it, GitHub gets a tracking issue, Slack notifies the on-call channel.
templates.customer-escalation-router.des: Webhook receives a complaint, AI classifies severity, and condition-guarded edges fan out to one of three escalation branches: low (Slack ping), medium (GitHub issue + Slack), or high (human review + GitHub issue + urgent Slack alert).
templates.lead-enrichment-handoff.name: Lead enrichment → sales handoff
templates.lead-enrichment-handoff.descri: Webhook receives a marketing-form lead, AI scores and enriches it, and a condition routes qualified leads to Slack + a welcome email while unqualified leads receive a nurture-sequence email.
templates.refund-triage-approval.name: Refund triage → approval → billing webhook
templates.refund-triage-approval.descrip: Webhook receives a refund request, AI summarizes the claim, a human approval gate decides yes/no, then a signed webhook calls the billing system and an email confirms to the customer.
templates.ai-support-draft-review.name: AI support draft → human review → send
templates.ai-support-draft-review.descri: Webhook receives a support ticket, AI drafts a response, a human agent reviews/edits via a typed form, and the final reply is emailed to the customer.
templates.churn-risk-weekly-digest.name: Churn-risk weekly digest (scheduled)
templates.churn-risk-weekly-digest.descr: Cron-fires every Monday 9am, pulls at-risk users from a configured analytics endpoint, AI ranks them, then a digest message lands in Slack for the customer-success channel.
templates.email-reply.name: Email auto-reply
templates.email-reply.description: Skeleton for reading inbound email and sending a templated reply via email.send. Operator fills the trigger source and recipient details in the Inspector.
templates.failed-workflow-recovery.name: Failed workflow recovery → DLQ → patch → replay
templates.failed-workflow-recovery.descr: Headline recovery demo. A webhook fires a write-side billing call that is intentionally broken in two ways: no approval gate upstream of the write, and a Bearer token referencing an unbound secret. The run lands in the Recovery Queue; the AI suggests both an upstream approval insertion (structural) and a swap_secret_ref fix (config). One demo, two recovery patterns.
templates.monthly-report-pdf.name: Monthly metrics report → PDF → email
templates.monthly-report-pdf.description: Scheduled cron fires on the first of each month, fetches metrics from an analytics endpoint, AI summarizes the top movers, pdf.generate renders a polished PDF, and email.send delivers it. Showcases schedule + http + ai + pdf + email in a single workflow.
templates.multi-agent-decision.name: Multi-agent decision support (debate + arbiter)
templates.multi-agent-decision.descripti: Webhook receives a decision prompt, three sequential agents debate the proposal — an optimist supports it, a skeptic critiques it, and an arbiter weighs both sides and writes the final recommendation.
templates.mcp-notion-summary.name: MCP Notion → AI summary → Slack
templates.mcp-notion-summary.description: Webhook receives a Notion page id, calls an external MCP server (alias notion-demo) to read the page, AI summarizes the contents, and Slack notifies the team. Showcases Janusly as an MCP client.
templates.bulk-classify-loop.name: Bulk customer classify → digest email
templates.bulk-classify-loop.description: Webhook receives a batch of customers, the loop primitive normalizes each one into a summary line, AI classifies the entire batch in a single grouped call, and email.send delivers the digest.
